title: Carbonate and sulfate minerals do not share the same acid-test signal
original_forecast: The carbonate route supplies inorganic carbon and potentially retained CO2; gypsum supplies calcium/sulfate without a stoichiometric carbon-gas source. Confirm gas identity from inventory rather than pressure alone.
original_limitations: Pressure also depends on headspace state and temperature. Gypsum dissolution is limited by equilibrium, not expected to match the carbonate sample's dissolution extent.

question.original_criterion: Can a gas observation distinguish a carbonate sample from gypsum without assuming that any dissolving white solid releases CO2?
question.original_instruction: The carbonate route supplies inorganic carbon and potentially retained CO2; gypsum supplies calcium/sulfate without a stoichiometric carbon-gas source. Confirm gas identity from inventory rather than pressure alone.
question.assessment: Carbonate contributes0.5 mmol additional inorganicC while gypsum contributes0.5 mmol sulfate; both retain separately counted airCO2. Actual gas identity/inventory, not pressure alone, distinguishes arms. Full original sealed C/Ca/S/H/O/Cl/N/charge closes every row, with actual temperature andnRT/V pressures. No carbonate dissolving trajectory or gypsum solubility equality is assumed.
